item.title: Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts
item.description: … Warn of burnout, stroke risks, seek healthier work environments By Chioma Obinna Health experts yesterday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks. The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients. They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives. Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations. Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.” She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles. “First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said. According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities. She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority. “Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said. The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments. She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation. Daniel further recommended accessible spaces for physical activity in workplaces, including walkways, trees and encouragement for workers to use stairs where appropriate. item.title: Foursquare G.O. tasks graduands on integrity, national development
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The General Overseer of the Foursquare Gospel Church in Nigeria, Rev. Sam Aboyeji, has charged graduating students of LIFE Theological Seminary, Ikorodu, Lagos, to uphold integrity and sound biblical doctrine as they prepare to preach the Gospel and contribute to society. Aboyeji gave the charge at the institution’s 2026 graduation ceremony, where he urged the graduands to see their graduation not as an end but as a stepping stone to greater responsibilities in God’s service. Speaking on the theme of the ceremony, “Trailblazers,” and drawing from Titus 2:7-8, the cleric said the credibility of their future ministries would depend largely on the integrity of their personal lives. He said: “You have been equipped with knowledge and skills that must now find expression in faithful service to God and humanity. I charge you to distinguish yourselves as trailblazers whose lives exemplify the sound doctrine you have received.” Quoting Apostle Paul’s admonition to Titus, Aboyeji urged the graduates to be examples of good works, demonstrating integrity in doctrine, reverence, incorruptible speech and soundness of character. He warned against compromising biblical truths in the face of challenges, urging them to remain courageous, steadfast and diligent in their ministerial responsibilities. “Be courageous in breaking new ground, steadfast in the face of challenges, uncompromising in matters of biblical truth, and diligent in the discharge of your ministerial responsibilities,” he said. Reminding the graduands that service to God was a sacred responsibility requiring accountability to the Creator, the General Overseer urged them to remain worthy ambassadors of LIFE Theological Seminary and vessels of honour in their respective fields of assignment. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Governing Council of LIFE Theological Seminary, Rev. Joe Ameh, urged the graduating class to distinguish themselves as trailblazers and uncompromising ambassadors of Christ in a society increasingly challenged by moral decay and corruption. Ameh said the graduates were expected to demonstrate the values of Christianity and apply their theological training in addressing contemporary issues in a rapidly changing society. He said: “As trailblazers, those of you graduating today are expected to be ardent and passionate in distinguishing yourselves before a world characterised by normlessness and anomie. item.title: Blindness: Eritrea, 10 others eliminate trachoma from Africa as Nigeria lags
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Eritrea has become the 11th country in the World Health Organisation (WHO) African Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem, raising hopes of ending a neglected tropical disease (NTD) that continues to threaten the sight of millions of people across the continent. The achievement, validated by WHO, places Eritrea among 11 African countries that have successfully tackled the disease through sustained public health interventions, improved access to treatment, hygiene promotion and community mobilisation. Eritrea joins Algeria, Benin, Burundi, Eritrea, The Gambia, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Senegal and Togo as the African countries that have received WHO validation as the number of countries that have achieved elimination globally stands at 34. Eritrea is also the 66th country globally and the 23rd in the WHO African Region to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease. According to WHO, Eritrea achieved the milestone, following two decades of sustained interventions targeting the disease, particularly in remote rural communities where poor access to clean water, sanitation and healthcare had fuelled its spread. Eritrea’s success followed nationwide surveys conducted between 2006 and 2020, which helped identify affected communities and guide the rollout of interventions across the country. The government subsequently implemented WHO’s recommended SAFE strategy, a combination of surgery for advanced cases, antibiotics to clear infection, facial cleanliness to limit transmission and environmental improvements, particularly better access to water and sanitation. A notable feature of the campaign was its community-led sanitation approach, which delivered significant public health gains despite limited external funding. Health workers deployed digital tools for data collection and mapping to identify affected populations, track disease patterns and direct resources to hard-to-reach communities. In a congratulatory message, WHO Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, “I congratulate the Government and people of Eritrea on this historic achievement. After two decades of determined effort, Eritrea has consigned trachoma as a public health problem to history. This is a victory for the communities most affected by this devastating disease, and a powerful example of what sustained national commitment can achieve.” On his part, WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said Eritrea’s achievement demonstrated the impact of political commitment, community participation and effective partnerships in tackling neglected tropical diseases. “I congratulate Eritrea on this historic public health milestone. It shows what is possible through sustained political commitment, community leadership and strong partnerships. item.title: Eyesan seeks more opportunities for women in petroleum sector
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Commission Chief Executive, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has called for greater opportunities for women in the petroleum sector. Eyesan made the call on Wednesday while speaking on the topic, “Breaking Barriers,” at the 2026 Women in NNPC Limited (WIN) in Abuja, under the theme, “Powered by Her.” She asked women to also prioritise competence, resilience and continuous learning as critical tools for breaking barriers. A statement by the Commission said Eyesan urged women not to be discouraged by delayed promotions, stressing that professional growth requires patience, perseverance and commitment to excellence. Sharing her personal experience, Eyesan disclosed that she spent eight years in the same position without promotion but remained committed to her career. Eyesan also emphasised the importance of involving men in conversations about gender inclusion and women’s advancement, noting that some of the major milestones in her career were made possible by men who recognised her competence and provided opportunities. “I was appointed the first female Head of Strategy, not by a woman, but by a man who believed in my competence. I was also appointed as the first female EVP Upstream, NNPCL, by a man who believed in my competence, and today I stand as the first female CCE of NUPRC by Mr President, who is a man who believes that I will deliver,” she said. Acknowledging the gradual increase in opportunities for women in the industry, the NUPRC boss called for more deliberate efforts to achieve meaningful representation, advocating at least 25 per cent participation of women in leadership and decision-making positions. “Is it happening at the scale we want? Not quite, we need more. At least one in four. Not just because we want to make up the numbers but because we think we bring value to the table,” she said. The NUPRC boss also commended the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr Bayo Ojulari, for the WIN initiative, describing it as a valuable platform for positioning young women for greater opportunities and leadership roles in the oil and gas industry. She noted that the Nigerian oil and gas industry was recording significant progress through collaboration between the regulator, NNPC Limited and other industry operators. item.title: American strategist denies receiving $4.5m for Tinubu interview
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government for her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London, in a post on her X account on Wednesday night, described the allegation as a smear campaign, insisting that neither the Nigerian government nor anyone else in the country paid her the reported sum. She said her visit to Nigeria was to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to see the country for herself. “I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself. “This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she wrote. The denial comes amid controversy surrounding her interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday, and reports alleging that she was linked to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government in the United States. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar had called on the Presidency to clarify whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying contract and disclose the details of the arrangement. In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal. He said the filings indicated that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but maintained that the Presidency should clarify whether the interview formed part of the contract. Atiku demanded the publication of the contract, details of the payment and the release of the full, unedited recording of the interview. He also questioned the nature of the engagement, arguing that the Presidency should establish whether the encounter was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement. The former vice president further asked the government to disclose who authorised the payment, the source of the funds and whether public money was involved. The controversy followed London’s earlier social media posts praising the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and US President Donald Trump. In one of the posts, she described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, saying the security cooperation between both countries was producing results and could create further economic and trade opportunities. She also expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria in efforts to strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. item.title: 2026 Globe Soccer Awards: Messi, Ronaldo, Dembele, Yamal included [Full List]
item.description: Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Lamine Yamal are among the high-profile footballers nominated for the 2026 Beyond Developments Globe Soccer Awards. The nominees for the 17th edition of the awards were unveiled on Wednesday through the organisers’ official website, with Paris Saint-Germain and Spain among the prominent names following their successes in the UEFA Champions League and 2026 FIFA World Cup. Dembele, who won the Best Men’s Player award last year, has been shortlisted again alongside 25 other players for the individual prize. Meanwhile, Ronaldo will be seeking to retain the Best Middle East Player award after making the 2026 shortlist. The awards ceremony is billed for December 28 in the United Arab Emirates, while public voting across 12 categories commenced on Wednesday and will end on November 30. The organisers disclosed that fans would determine the first round of voting, with their votes combined with those of the Globe Soccer Jury during the second round. The jury features several prominent former football figures, including Marcello Lippi, Antonio Conte, Iker Casillas and Luis Figo. The previous edition attracted more than 30 million votes from over 200 countries and territories. According to the organisers, supporters can cast their votes through the official website, vote.globesoccer.com, or the Globe Soccer mobile application. item.title: 2027: SDP pledges free education, vows to tackle insecurity
item.description: …Promises N200 petrol, affordable housing, jobs By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has pledged to tackle poverty, insecurity, unemployment and other socio-economic challenges facing Nigerians if elected into power in the 2027 general elections. The party said addressing poverty and economic hardship was critical to tackling insecurity, insurgency, kidnapping and other criminal activities across the country. Speaking on Wednesday at the SDP presidential campaign rally in Yola, Adamawa State, the party’s National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, urged Nigerians to make informed political choices ahead of the 2027 elections, saying poverty and insecurity required purposeful leadership and people-oriented policies. Gombe urged residents to support the party’s presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and his running mate, Professor Usman Bugaje, saying the ticket was committed to addressing the country’s challenges through policies that would create economic opportunities, improve living conditions and restore public confidence in governance. In a statement issued on Wednesday by the National Coordinator of the SDP Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Yunusa Tanko, the party chairman urged Adamawa residents to assess the records, character and policy proposals of candidates before deciding whom to support in the 2027 elections. In his remarks, the presidential candidate, Adebayo, said an SDP-led administration would redefine governance by ensuring that public resources were deployed for the benefit of Nigerians, with priority given to security, education, healthcare, housing, food security and employment. Describing the SDP as a party founded on democratic values and social justice, he said its philosophy was anchored on the belief that political power belonged to the people and that government resources must be used to improve their welfare. He said his proposed administration would focus on implementing the fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy contained in Chapter Two of the Constitution, particularly provisions relating to poverty reduction and citizens’ welfare. “Government is the organisation selected by you through your votes. Government must provide security, accountability, good food, affordable housing, quality education and accessible healthcare. It must work for the people who elected it,” he said. On security, Adebayo identified terrorism, banditry and kidnapping as some of Nigeria’s most pressing challenges, promising decisive measures to address them through improved security management and better support for security personnel. item.title: ADC leaders lazy, entitled politicians – NDC campaign DG
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, National Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkareem, Wednesday, said some leaders of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, as lazy and entitled politicians. Abdulkareem also said they had failed to establish clear terms for the coalition they were seeking to build. He faulted the ADC leaders for failing to agree on power-sharing arrangements and a presidential candidate before bringing politicians into the coalition, saying the North should not continue to dominate the country’s leadership. Speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, he said: “I used to term some of the people I see in ADC as lazy politicians. Right from time, even when they are constructing this coalition that they talk about, instead of them finding a way of doing what the All Progressives Congress, APC, had done, put everything in black and white that we want to come for a coalition. And this coalition, this is the person that we want to be the president, or we are zoning this part of what we are going to do to this part of the country. “At that time, everybody that is coming into that coalition knows exactly why he’s coming, so it’s not going to be any problem in trying to see who becomes what. Immediately we started this thing they started to say Peter Obi is a vice-presidential candidate to Atiku. What kind of coalition is that? The entitlement from the elite, I find it very annoying sometimes. “You just decide the North. Which North? You talk like you own something that you. There is no right given to Atiku, for example, to say everybody must surrender. We have been ruling from Gen Ibrahim Babangida (retd) to the late Muhammadu Buhari. But look at where we are. “Go and see our streets. Go and see our villages. Look at how we have been ravaged. But since somebody is still coming today, trying to play this northern card at this level, it’s time to start thinking how can we hire somebody, irrespective of where he’s coming from, irrespective of religion or tribe, somebody that we know he has this integrity, somebody that can make these public funds to be used for public good, somebody that can be accountable, not people that are old and full of entitlement.” The post ADC leaders lazy, entitled politicians – NDC campaign DG appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lagos-Ibadan Expressway gridlock leaves commuters stranded for hours
item.description: Motorists and commuters were stranded for several hours on Wednesday following the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, which triggered a massive traffic gridlock. The congestion paralysed movement on both sides of the expressway, with motorists travelling towards Lagos held up from the Redemption Camp area to Aseese bus stop, while those heading towards Ogun State were trapped from the Long Bridge area to Aseese. The scale of the gridlock left commuters spending unusually long hours on journeys that would ordinarily take a fraction of the time. One of our correspondents, who boarded a commercial vehicle from Ibadan shortly after 11am, did not arrive in Magboro, Ogun State, until about 5.30pm. Another motorist lamented spending eight hours travelling from Mowe to Magboro, highlighting the severity of the traffic situation. The gridlock persisted as late as 10pm, with both sections of the expressway reportedly almost completely blocked. Efforts by some motorists to escape the congestion by driving against the flow of traffic further compounded the situation, as they obstructed vehicles moving in the appropriate lanes. With vehicular movement severely restricted, commercial motorcyclists cashed in on the situation, making brisk business by conveying stranded commuters through alternative routes. The renewed construction work on the pedestrian bridge at Aseese was identified as the immediate trigger of the traffic disruption. The post Lagos-Ibadan Expressway gridlock leaves commuters stranded for hours appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FIFA picks Amokachi, four others to oversee NFF until May 2027
item.description: World football governing body FIFA has appointed former Super Eagles striker Daniel Amokachi and four others to a five-member normalisation committee tasked with overseeing the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF). The committee will be chaired by former NFF electoral committee chairman Sampson Ebomhe and is expected to manage the federation’s transition and organise fresh elections for a new leadership. Its mandate will run until May 31, 2027, at the latest. FIFA communicated the appointments in a letter sent to the NFF secretariat on Wednesday, following consultations with the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Other members of the committee are governance expert Dr Joe Abah, veteran sports journalist and administrator Godwin Enakhena, and Amina Yerima. “We refer to the decision of the Bureau of the FIFA Council of 22 October 2026 to appoint a normalisation committee for the Nigeria Football Federation. “In this respect, following consultation with CAF, we hereby communicate the composition of the normalisation committee as follows: Mr Sampson Ebomhe (chairman), Dr Joe Abah (member), Mr Godwin Enakhena (member), Ms Amina Yerima (member) and Mr Daniel Amokachi (member),” the letter read. The world football governing body said the appointees would commence their duties immediately, subject to eligibility screening by its Review Committee in line with FIFA Governance Regulations. Their final confirmation will depend on the outcome of the screening exercise. FIFA also prohibited members of the committee from contesting any position in the forthcoming NFF elections, regardless of whether they resign or have their appointments revoked. “None of the members of the normalisation committee will be eligible for the positions to be filled during the upcoming NFF elections under any circumstances, including in the event that their mandate as a member of the normalisation committee is revoked or that they resign from their position,” the letter added. FIFA further stated that it could, in consultation with CAF, withdraw the appointment of any committee member or expand the committee by appointing additional members. The intervention follows the resignation of NFF President Ibrahim Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s executive committee on August 27, 2026, amid growing criticism of the country’s football administration. The development disrupted arrangements for the NFF elective congress scheduled for September 27, prompting FIFA and CAF to step in and approve the establishment of a normalisation committee to supervise the transition. Ebomhe, who will lead the committee, has previously held several positions in Nigerian sports administration. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Can’t Alter State Police Bill, He’ll Definitely Sign It — Omole
item.description: Lawyer and author Charles Omole has said that he does not expect President Bola Tinubu to make an alteration to the National Policing Bill transmitted to him by the National Assembly. Omole, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday. He explained that altering the bill would return the process to the Senate, House of Representatives and state houses of assembly for their approval. Omole noted further that the constitutional amendment is not the meat and bone of policing but simply allows state police to exist, while the National Policing Bill specifies the structure and functions of the state police. He, however, said that the National Policing Bill could not be considered until the constitutional amendment had gone through. He explained that while the 36 states would have their own police service, the police in the Federal Capital Territory would be under the control of the federal police service. Omole, however, said that part of the recommendation under the bill is that states cannot buy their own arms and ammunition at will. item.title: Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Kephas Ropshik, on Wednesday said that Governor Caleb Mutfwang performed poorly in governance in the state. Ropshik, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , said the governor had not scored more than 20 per cent in performance. The PDP candidate said that leadership should be about performance and about the people. “In fact, I can tell you on a scale of one to 100, you can give him like 15 to 20 per cent in performance,” he said. “He still remains someone that I respect, but of course that, completely, is different from politics.” ﻿ He alleged that the governor defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) when he could not cope with the crisis in the PDP. He, however, said that the governor did not leave with up to 15 per cent of the members of the PDP, insisting that Plateau is a PDP state. “You know, a man’s strength and leadership qualities are being tested when there are crises, but the governor couldn’t stand the crisis. He left for APC, and so there was an opening in the PDP to contest for governorship because, of course, the truth is this. Plateau has been a PDP state. “You can’t take that away from Plateau State, right? And so there was a vacancy, and so somebody needed to fill in the gap. And so even with the crisis, we believed in the PDP,” the candidate said. “Mutfwang did not live with 15, 20 per cent of people, I mean, in PDP to APC. The people, in fact, not even 10 per cent, because the people that followed him to APC are his appointees, and that’s the truth. “Ninety per cent of people on the Plateau still believe in the PDP.” Ropshik said that Plateau is one of the frontrunners in the Rainbow Coalition. He also said that he was working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. Asked whether he was not confusing his followers by telling them to vote for the APC in the January 16 presidential election, and the PDP in the February 6, 2027 governorship election in the state, Ropshik said, “No, no, no, I am not reading because now if we want to be sincere to ourselves, the PDP presidential candidate, we all know that there’s no chance for him to win the election. “And so why should we now waste the votes? We must find a platform to identify; what we’re after is good governance.” The post Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, Niger reach deal on military pursuit of terrorists
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Nigeria and three neighbouring countries — Cameroon, Chad and Niger — have reportedly agreed to allow military forces to pursue terrorists, armed bandits and other criminal groups up to five kilometres across their shared borders. The arrangement is aimed at strengthening regional counterterrorism operations and preventing fleeing militants from escaping military pressure by crossing into neighbouring territories. The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed the agreement in Abuja, explaining that it would enable security forces to sustain hot pursuit of fleeing terrorists across border areas. The agreement is expected to strengthen military cooperation among the four countries, particularly in tackling transnational security threats posed by Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and other armed criminal groups operating around the Lake Chad Basin and adjoining border communities. Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was receiving real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training support from the United States to enhance its counterterrorism capabilities and improve the effectiveness of military operations. The Defence Minister said Nigerian troops had recently neutralised several terrorist and bandit commanders during overnight operations across the North-East and North-West regions. He said the cross-border pursuit arrangement is particularly significant for communities along Nigeria’s borders with Cameroon, Chad and Niger, where terrorist groups have exploited porous boundaries to evade security operations and sustain their activities. In Cameroon’s Far North Region, Boko Haram and ISWAP activities have continued to pose security challenges, making closer military coordination between neighbouring countries critical to addressing the threat. Details of the agreement, including its operational procedures, rules of engagement and safeguards for civilians in affected border communities, have not been provided in the information released. The arrangement signals a renewed push for regional military cooperation, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations against terrorist networks whose activities extend beyond national boundaries. item.title: Gun can kill terrorists, only education can kill terrorism – Buratai
item.description: The former Chief of Army Staff, retired Lt.-Gen. Tukur Buratai has called for inclusive education and wider access to learning opportunities, saying they are critical to addressing the conditions that sustain terrorism and violent extremism in Nigeria. Buratai made the call at the 2026 Young Adult Literature Prize Award and unveiling of the 2025 anthology of the T.Y. Buratai Literary Initiative (TYBLI), on Wednesday in Nasarawa State. The former Nigerian Ambassador to Benin Republic said military force alone could not defeat terrorism without deliberate investment in education, intellectual development and the minds of young Nigerians. “Gun can kill a terrorist, but only education can kill terrorism,” he declared. Buratai said national development must go beyond infrastructure, military strength and economic resources to include the intellectual capacity, creative imagination and moral consciousness of citizens. He stressed that young Nigerians, irrespective of their backgrounds, needed equal opportunities, platforms and encouragement to develop their talents and contribute meaningfully to society. The former COAS said the initiative was established on the conviction that great nations were built not only by strong armies and economies but also by ideas, literature and educated citizens. He urged universities to promote young adult literature through research, teaching and programmes that encouraged creativity, critical thinking and intellectual development. “A school that produces excellent academic results but neglects imagination and critical thinking has not fully prepared its students for the future,” he said. Buratai said the initiative had, since 2023, provided a platform for young Nigerians from diverse backgrounds to demonstrate their creativity and move from passive consumption to active production of literature. He described the unveiling of the 2025 anthology as another milestone, providing a permanent record of the imagination, creativity and achievements of young authors. He also announced plans to introduce full scholarships for deserving winners within the next three to five years, to enable them to complete their education. In a goodwill message, the Vice-Chancellor of Nasarawa State University, Keffi, Prof. Sa’adatu Liman, described young adult literature as an important bridge between childhood and adulthood. Liman said literature helped young people confront questions of identity, courage, faith, justice and leadership through stories that reflected their experiences. She described the initiative as an investment in human development and nation-building, pledging the university’s readiness to strengthen its partnership with TYBLI. Also, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Prof. Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, commended the initiative for recognising the importance of academic leadership, scholarship and research mentorship. item.title: FAAC shares N2.4trn among FG, states, LGs for October
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) has shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government. The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja on Wednesday. The N2.441 trillion comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.688 trillion and Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N752.488 billion. A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) indicated that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026. Total deduction for cost of collection was N128.797 billion while total transfers, refunds and savings stood at N1.241 trillion. According to the communiqué sent to media houses by Bawa Mokwa, Director of Press of the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, Wednesday night, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026. This was lower than the sum of N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion. Gross revenue of N812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426 billion. The communiqué stated that from the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of N809.909 billion. The Local Government Councils received N568.701 billion, while the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue. On the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion and the State Governments received N396.040 billion. The Local Government Councils received N305.331 billion and the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue. From the N752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, the State Governments received N413.868 billion and the Local Government Councils received N263.371 billion. In October 2026, Excise Duty and CET Levies increased marginally, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased. The post FAAC shares N2.4trn among FG, states, LGs for October appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Approves Establishment Of University Of Public Relations, Leadership
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of the University of Public Relations, Leadership, the first of its kind to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations. Tinubu announced this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum and the 51st Africa Public Relations Association Conference in Abuja on Wednesday. He also described it as a forward-looking investment in human capital and the future of the communication profession. The President also said it would provide an opportunity to develop a new generation of communication leaders equipped to respond to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment. “An important outcome of hosting this forum is our determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession,” Tinubu, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, said. “In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership.” He urged investors to explore Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage, tourism assets and the ingenuity of the Nigerian people. “ Naija no go carry last ! Nigeria is a country of enormous possibilities. We are a nation of diverse cultures, talents and ideas, with a youthful population, a dynamic private sector and a strong determination to build a more prosperous future,” he added. item.title: ADC, Kaduna gov’t differ over venue
item.description: From Mohammed Ibrahim Yaba, Kaduna; Hussein Yahaya, Baba Martins & Daniel Adaji, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Kaduna State Government of denying the party the use of the Ranchers Bees Stadium to host the Northwest rally of its presidential campaign. The party said it had applied to use the stadium for its rally scheduled for November 17 and 18 but was refused access to the facility by the state government, which denied the claim. The ADC National Vice Chairman, North-West, Hafsat Baba, told one of our correspondents that the party dutifully informed the state government of its intention to use the facility, but the latter turned down its request. Daily Trust reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC) recently held its presidential campaign flag-off at the same venue. In a letter dated November 12, 2026 reportedly from the Kaduna State Ministry of Local Government Affairs and addressed to the Office of the National Vice Chairman of the ADC, North-West, the ministry said the stadium would not be available on the requested dates due to ongoing repairs. The letter, signed by Mohammed Sani Haruna, Senior Special Assistant to the Commissioner, stated: “We write to acknowledge receipt of your letter with the above caption. However, we regret to inform you that due to ongoing repairs at the stadium, it will not be available for the aforementioned programme on the dates requested by you.” Baba said the ADC also notified security agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Inspector-General of Police, Kaduna State Police Command and the General Officer Commanding, about the planned rally. “We sent these letters not only to state security agencies but also to their national offices, just to be on the safe side,” she said. Baba explained that the party initially considered the Ahmadu Bello Stadium but was informed that it was under construction and subsequently considered the Trade Fair Complex but was also told that the facility would not be available. She said the party decided to request Ranchers Bees Stadium after learning that the APC had recently used it for its presidential campaign flag-off. “We were aware that Ahmadu Bello Stadium was under construction. We then thought of using the Trade Fair Complex, but we were made to understand that it would also not be available. We knew that they (APC) used Ranchers Bees recently, so we decided to request it, but it was denied,” she said. The ADC chieftain questioned why its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, should be prevented from holding a rally in Kaduna, which she described as his second home. “If Atiku can visit Bauchi and Yobe and hold his rallies, why can’t he come to Kaduna, his second home, because he has a house here?” she asked.
